articles.title: Refuerzos interiores para el Barça ante la llegada de Valanciunas
articles.standfirst: Nebo y Evbuomwan se entrenan con el grupo y podrían tener minutos ante el Zalgiris mientras Minaya tendrá que estar 10 días de baja por una lesión en el aductor del muslo derecho
articles.summary: Nebo y Evbuomwan se entrenan con el grupo y podrían tener minutos ante el Zalgiris mientras Minaya tendrá que estar 10 días de baja por una lesión en el aductor del muslo derecho
articles.body: Movimientos en la enfermería del Barcelona. Salen dos y entra uno. Quienes han recibido el alta son los interiores Josh Nebo y Tosan Evbuomwan, que ya se han entrenado con el resto del equipo y podrían estar listos para jugar este viernes en la visita del Zalgiris. Y el que ha caído es Justin Minaya, que ha sufrido una lesión en el aductor del muslo derecho y estará unos 10 días de baja. Su ausencia se suma a la de Yoan Makoundou, que se recupera de una agudización de una tendinopatía rotuliana en la rodilla izquierda. Los regresos de Nebo y Evbuomwan, que todavía se tendrán que confirmar este viernes, serían una gran noticia para el conjunto azulgrana. Primero, porque Olek Balcerowski ha comenzado la temporada como único pívot sano. Y, segundo, porque se van a necesitar refuerzos ante la llegada del Zalgiris con uno de los mejores interiores de la Euroliga: Jonas Valanciunas. El pívot lituano de 34 años y 2,11 metros ha regresado a Europa después de 14 temporadas y 1.002 encuentros en la NBA. En tres jornadas ya ha marcado territorio: 12,0 puntos, 6,7 rebotes, 3,0 asistencias, 2,3 tapones y 20,3 créditos de valoración por encuentro. Es el noveno jugador más valorado de la competición. Aleksander Sekulic considera que "el Zalgiris no es sólo Valanciunas, que es un gran jugador y tiene una carrera increíble. Su equipo está jugando un buen baloncesto. Esta temporada, por ejemplo, tiene una victoria y dos derrotas, pero podría haber ganado los dos partidos que perdió". Los lituanos cayeron por poco ante el Olympiacos (91-93) y el París Basketball (82-78). Y atención, porque el equipo de Kaunas es el único que tiene a dos efectivos en el Top 10 de valoración. Azuolas Tubelis, un ala-pívot de 2,08 metros y 24 años, está confirmando lo bueno que ya mostró el curso pasado y en el inicio del actual es una de las grandes sensaciones de la Euroliga: 15,7 puntos y 8,7 rebotes, líder de la estadística, para 23,3 de valoración. El Barça, con un balance de 2-1 después de las tres primeras jornadas, tratará de hacerse fuerte en el Palau, donde remontó al Anadolu Efes en el único partido que ha disputado hasta ahora en casa en competición europea (89-82).

articles.title: Cooper Flagg Unveils Signature Logo with New Balance in New Photo Ahead of 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: Two weeks before opening his second NBA season, Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg has unveiled his new signature logo.
articles.body:
Two weeks before opening his second NBA season, Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg has unveiled his new signature logo.

During an event in China prior to the Mavs' preseason game in Macau, Flagg revealed the "CF" logo that will be featured on his New Balance merchandise.

Flagg took some inspiration from his home state of Maine by making the C look like a pine tree.

The Eastern White Pine is the official state tree of Maine. Since 90 percent of Maine is forestland, it has earned the nickname of the "Pine Tree State."

Prior to his lone season at Duke, Flagg signed an endorsement deal with New Balance. He joined the stable of basketball players with the company, along with Kawhi Leonard, Kyrie Irving and Zach LaVine.

Flagg does not currently have a signature shoe, but he was given his own personal colorway of the New Balance Hesi Low v2 that he wore throughout his rookie season.

Selected with the No. 1 pick in the 2025 NBA draft, Flagg managed to live up to all of the hype he had coming into the league as a rookie. He averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game in 70 starts for the Mavericks.

Flagg joined Michael Jordan as the only rookies since the 1973-74 season to lead their team in total points, rebounds, assists and steals.

The Mavs will tipoff their preseason schedule Friday against the Houston Rockets in the first of two games at the Venetian Arena.

Flagg and the Mavericks will begin the 2026-27 regular season on Oct. 21 against the Rockets at the Toyota Center.

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg Hyped by Kerr Ahead of Rookie Season, 'One of Our Best Players Already'
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg is on track to get significant playing time during his rookie NBA season.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg is on track to get significant playing time during his rookie NBA season.

Warriors coach Steve Kerr told ESPN's Anthony Slater Lendeborg is "going to play a ton."

"Frankly, he deserves it," Kerr said, per Slater. "He's one of our best players already."

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

Players With the Most to Prove This Season 🏀

Slater's report comes shortly after Lendeborg posted 17 points, nine rebounds and two assists while starting for the Warriors in a preseason blowout of the Los Angeles Lakers.

Lendeborg has spent time in both preseason and training camp as part of a potential starting five alongside Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Draymond Green and Al Horford.

When asked last week by Bonta Hill and Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports' Dubs Talk Podcast if Lendeborg was the "most pro-ready rookie" he'd had on his roster as the Warriors coach, Kerr answered, "Yeah, 100 percent."

"He's the most prepared, most ready guy," Kerr told Hill and Johnson. "I think he was coached really well last year by Dusty May."

Kerr added Lendeborg's biggest focus should be improving his "defensive awareness" heading into his first NBA campaign.

The Warriors coach has previously said he wants Lendeborg to also be more aggressive on offense, a message that has been echoed by Green.

Green said on an Oct. 4 episode of his podcast players like Lendeborg and Jimmy Butler "see the floor so well that when you want them to have tunnel vision and go score" they sometimes focus more on passing opportunities.

Lendeborg was selected by the Warriors with the No. 11 pick of the 2026 draft. After beginning his college career at Arizona Western College, he transferred to UAB and then to Michigan, where he averaged 15.1 points and 6.8 rebounds during the Wolverines' run to a national title.

Kerr will hope what he described as a "chip" on Lendeborg's shoulder from his beginning as an unranked JUCO prospect will help the rookie continue developing on both ends of the court as he prepares to tip off his first regular season Oct. 21 at the Los Angeles Lakers.

articles.title: SGA's Trainer Reveals Text Thunder Star Sent After Watching Knicks Win 2026 NBA Title
articles.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander may have gained some extra motivation to lead the Oklahoma City Thunder back to title contention by watching the New York Knicks lift the Larry O'Brien Trophy.
articles.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander may have gained some extra motivation to lead the Oklahoma City Thunder back to title contention by watching the New York Knicks lift the Larry O'Brien Trophy.

Trainer Nem Ilic told RG.org's Mark Medina he received a text from Gilgeous-Alexander just before the Knicks clinched the 2026 title in Game 5 against the San Antonio Spurs.

"I'm pissed. I can't believe I'm not here right now," Gilgeous-Alexander texted Ilic, per Medina.

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

Gilgeous-Alexander then began working on scheduling on-court workouts with Ilic, according to Medina.

Ilic told Medina, "We were on vacation right around when Games 1 and 2 started. We watched that together. But I didn't get that same vibe until the series was actually over.

"Then it hit him that they lost and New York won the championship... He knew that he had to get back to the drawing board and get better again."

The Thunder lost the Western Conference Finals and the chance to defend their 2025 title despite Gilgeous-Alexander posting 35 points in Game 7 against the Spurs. Gilgeous-Alexander was apparently vacationing by the time Spurs tipped off the championship series against the Knicks four days later.

The Thunder parted ways this offseason with players including Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins amid the franchise's apparent goal of staying under the second luxury tax apron.

Gilgeous-Alexander will hope players like Cason Wallace, Jared McCain and Ajay Mitchell can step up as the Thunder look to remain a contender this season, starting with an Oct. 20 conference finals rematch at the Spurs.

articles.title: How the Golden State Valkyries' historic defense has them on brink of WNBA Finals berth
articles.summary: The Valkyries have taken a commanding 2-0 series lead over the Aces behind their stellar defense.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — Whenever Chelsea Gray receives an inbound pass, she knows she'll likely be met with limbs. Taller limbs. Longer limbs.

Sometimes it's Kayla Thornton, the Golden State Valkyries' starter at the 4. It might be Cecilia Zandalasini, known less for her defense and more for her back-breaking, end-of-clock turnaround jumpers.

It could be Kaila Charles, an energetic reserve who may be overqualified for that role at this point. Maybe it's former Las Vegas Aces teammate Tiffany Hayes, whose pressure can force one to dribble off their own foot.

Regardless of the participant, Gray has to deal with it. Over, and over, and over again.

"Nobody likes to get picked up full-court," Aces head coach Becky Hammon told Yahoo Sports when asked about the Valkyries' high pick-up points ahead of Game 2, which Golden State would win 83-81 to take a 2-0 series lead on Wednesday.

As disruptive (another descriptor used by Hammon) as that early pressure can be, it's only the beginning.

The Valkyries' pressure ramps up in the half-court. Off-ball actions are stifled by early prep work and tons of (legal) physicality. On-ball defenders are in the jersey of whoever is tasked with initiating offense for the Aces, hounding them while they wait for something to open up.

When it isn't Gray dealing with it, it's likely Jackie Young — one of the league's elite who has looked like a shell of herself in this series.

Once it's time for a ball screen, the Aces often find themselves at a disadvantage:

They don't know if they'll win at the point-of-attack.

They don't know what coverage is coming from the big involved.

In the event they solve the first two, there's likely going to be a help defender (or two, or three) waiting on them.

Because of the early pressure, they've likely lost valuable time on the shot clock to figure it out.

This is how the Aces, headlined by the (future) GOAT in A'ja Wilson, fueled by the dynamic play of Young, guided by the steady hand of Gray, find themselves in the mud.

"For us, it's constantly making sure that they're off-rhythm," Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase told reporters after Game 2.

"Being able to utilize our numbers, keeping that type of energy, that type of ball pressure, that type of resistance and our shifts, is our focus. It really goes back to [controlling] what we can control … I feel like we really emptied the tank tonight."

An Aces team that finished second in offensive rating (112.9) — a top-five mark of all time — has struggled to crack 100 ( 97.2 through two ) in this series. And ultimately, that downturn in effectiveness is why they're heading back to Vegas facing a daunting 0-2 deficit.

It may be surprising to watch this particular trio — with all of the talent, the gravity, the championship experience — struggle the way they have. It shouldn't be a surprise that the Valkyries are the ones to force that struggle.

They weren't just the league's best defense this year, boasting a 99.1 defensive rating . They were nearly 10 points better than league average , making them (statistically) the stingiest defense in league history .

This roster is full of high-level defenders, but you have to start with their big three. Gabby Williams is coming off back-to-back top-three finishes in Defensive Player of the Year voting due to her on-ball peskiness and off-ball lurking. She's done a tremendous job of making Young uncomfortable in this series — and serving her buckets on the other end.

Kiah Stokes has long been an elite interior defender — and probably should've earned some DPOY love in her own right. Her work against Wilson has been superb; per Second Spectrum, Wilson is a whopping 7-of-19 (36.8%) on shots contested by Stokes. And in general, she just seems to be in the right place when you need her:

Her pick-and-roll work in tandem with Williams (guarding Young) has also been impactful, particularly when asked to switch. Through two games, the Aces haven't scored on a possession where Stokes has switched onto Young after a ball screen.

Then there's Veronica Burton, the Valkyries' point-of-attack maestro. While she's gotten cracks at pestering Young or Gray, she's also, notably, been given the Bri Turner assignment through the first two games.

It's a fun bit of cross-matching from Nakase, a downstream effect of wanting to put more length on Gray. It unlocks Burton as a roamer, giving her freedom to plug driving lanes and ultimately cramp space for the Aces.

"It's like a mini one-man zone," Hammon said .

It also puts Burton in spots that guards aren't usually accustomed to, with a mental checklist that deviates from the norm.

It may be cool to roam off a big early in a possession, for example, but there's a responsibility to make sure that big doesn't get busy on the glass.

"Well, I didn't rebound tonight," Burton said with a chuckle. "But there's an attention to detail in boxing out a big opposed to a guard. Especially at the point guard position, because a lot of times point guards have to get back on defense."

Hammon noted ahead of Game 2 that there could be opportunities for Turner to counter Burton's roaming with more aggression on the offensive glass.

To Burton's credit, she ended up logging 12 box-outs in Game 2, per Second Spectrum — a postseason high, and just the sixth time all season that she logged at least 10 in a game. Turner didn't record an offensive rebound in Game 2, and has only one for the series.

When you have tone-setters like Williams, Stokes and Burton, it makes it easier for everyone to fall in line.

Thornton doesn't mind hounding a future Hall of Fame point guard 60+ feet from the basket. Charles, Hayes and Zandalasini can do the same. A youngster like Aminata Gueye can come in and defend Wilson without fear, like we saw in Game 1.

The Aces made some tweaks in Game 2, notably sizing up by giving recently acquired Kalani Brown a postseason-high 23 minutes off the bench. She certainly produced, logging 9 points and 8 rebounds (3 OREB) and helping the Aces win her minutes by three.

With only a day between games, it'll be fascinating to see what other adjustments the Aces attempt to make to loosen things offensively and, ultimately, save their season. It's also worth monitoring if Jewell Loyd, who exited Game 1 and ultimately missed Game 2 with a leg injury, will make her return on Friday.

If the first two games are any indication, the Valkyries will be up for any challenge they face. With this kind of defense to lean on, why wouldn't they be?

articles.title: Lakers' Luka Doncic Takes Blame for Season-Ending Hamstring Injury, Missing 2026 NBA Playoffs
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is taking the blame for the hamstring injury that sidelined him for the Los Angeles Lakers' playoff run last spring.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is taking the blame for the hamstring injury that sidelined him for the Los Angeles Lakers' playoff run last spring.

Dončić played for the final time last season on April 2 against the Oklahoma City Thunder, a game in which the Lakers trailed by 31 points at the half.

He told Sports Illustrated 's Chris Mannix he regretted not exiting the game after tweaking his left hamstring in the second quarter.

Luka 'Had So Much Fun' Being Teammates with Bron

Dončić instead stayed in for the third, during which he suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain that kept him on the sideline for the rest of the season.

The Lakers were eliminated in a second-round sweep by the Thunder more than a month later.

"When it comes to my spirit of trying to win, I am just stubborn," Dončić told Mannix. "I felt a little bit in the first half that I should have just stopped. I should have come out. I think we had a team that could compete for the championship. I definitely regret it."

Dončić isn't the only player who showed up in the second half of that blowout loss to the Thunder only to miss significant time due to injury afterward.

Austin Reaves, who looked uncomfortable earlier in the game, started the third quarter before missing more than three weeks with an oblique injury.

Lakers coach JJ Redick told reporters after the game the Lakers had discussed at halftime whether to sit Dončić and Reaves, but ultimately decided to continue playing starters in an attempt to cut into the Thunder's lead.

Redick added Dončić had been checked out by team trainers at halftime before he was cleared to play in the second half.

"He got work done. He was cleared. Again, we're not going to put a player at risk. Those things happen," Redick said about Dončić in his postgame interview.

Dončić said in an August email to fans he had "100 percent" recovered from the hamstring injury.

Whether Dončić and Reaves can remain healthy this season will be key to their hopes of keeping a Lakers roster that has been completely overhauled in the wake of LeBron James' departure in playoff contention.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Sees 'A Lot of Joy' in Ja Morant After Trade to Trail Blazers from Grizzlies
articles.summary: The early returns for Ja Morant with the Portland Trail Blazers appear to be very positive.
articles.body:
The early returns for Ja Morant with the Portland Trail Blazers appear to be very positive.

Speaking to The Athletic's Jason Quick , Damian Lillard pointed out he has seen "a lot of joy" in Morant since he joined the Blazers after an offseason trade with the Memphis Grizzlies.

"I feel like he has a lot of joy right now," Lillard said. "I read people well, you know? And I can tell he is not pretending to be happy, you know? He walks around with a smile. And when we practice, and he's talking, he's engaged, he's invested, and you are able to see that he's happy with his situation."

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

Morant has hit a fascinating point in his career, needing to prove he can be an impact player again. He played a total of 79 games over his final three seasons with the Grizzlies.

The lack of availability helped contribute to Morant's trade value getting so low that Portland was able to acquire him from the Grizzlies in essentially a contract swap with Jerami Grant and Kris Murray going back to Memphis.

One thing that seemed to be missing for Morant at the end of his Memphis tenure was the athleticism and ability to attack the basket , but he looked good during the Blazers' fan fest on Sunday when he won MVP of the Black-Grey game.

Wednesday marked the first time Morant and Lillard played together in an official game when the Blazers kicked off their preseason schedule against the Golden State Warriors.

Morant finished with eight points, five assists and two steals in 19 minutes. Lillard, playing in his first game since tearing his Achilles on April 27, 2025, put up 15 points on 5-of-11 shooting in 19 minutes.

Blazers head coach Micah Nori used both Morant and Lillard in the starting lineup, though he has said he will tinker with the opening five throughout the preseason before deciding on the unit that will be used when the regular season begins.

The Blazers are hoping the addition of Morant and return of Lillard improves their fortunes in the Western Conference. They finished 42-40 last season and made the playoffs, losing as the No. 7 seed in the first round to the San Antonio Spurs, thanks to Deni Avdija's breakout campaign.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Commits to Future with Fever, Addresses 'EPIC' Contract Talks After WNBA Playoff Loss
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark affirmed her commitment to the organization as she becomes eligible for a massive extension this offseason.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark affirmed her commitment to the organization as she becomes eligible for a massive extension this offseason.

The new collective bargaining agreement introduced the Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract (EPIC) provision, which allows select players to get a max deal a year early.

During her exit interview Thursday, Clark told reporters she's undecided on whether she'll sign this winter under the EPIC provision, but that doesn't reflect anything bigger about her views on the Fever. Her focus is on identifying the best way to build a championship-caliber squad in Indiana:

In the NBA, stars typically get a rookie max extension at the earliest opportunity. Teams and players love the long-term security and certainty it provides.

The situation is a little different in the WNBA because the hard salary cap forces general managers to be more careful with the payroll.

Clark's earnings for 2027 would nearly triple if she re-signs now.

That's nearly $1 million less the Fever would have to spend on the rest of the roster when big changes could be ahead.

Four-time All-Star Kelsey Mitchell could be out the door. She didn't state outright she intends to leave Indy after nine seasons, but she said in her own exit interview that "I have to be selfish."

Replacing Mitchell would be difficult when there aren't many elite free agents hitting the market. That will be an issue even if the dynamic guard returns.

The Fever have two cornerstones in Clark and Aliyah Boston, who was the first player to sign the EPIC extension. Beyond that pair, general manager Amber Cox has a lot of work ahead to identity the additional pieces who can put Indiana over the top.

Clark seems to be aware of that challenge.

articles.title: Cinco jugadores heridos al caer desde un tercero el ascensor en el que viajaban
articles.standfirst: Parte de la plantilla del Gence BC azerbaiyano sufrió un accidente en la previa de su partido contra el Esenler Erokspor turco.
articles.summary: Parte de la plantilla del Gence BC azerbaiyano sufrió un accidente en la previa de su partido contra el Esenler Erokspor turco.
articles.body: Cinco jugadores del Gence BC, equipo azerbaiyano que participa en la FIBA Eurocup, resultaron heridos al caer desde una altura de tres pisos el ascensor en el que iban montados. Esa, según su entrenador Martin Knezevic, fue la principal causa de la derrota sufrida por 92-63 en la visita al Esenler Erokspor. Fue el técnico el que explicó su versión de los hechos en un mensaje en redes sociales cargado de ironía. "No me sorprendió en absoluto el resultado contra Erokspor, ya que anoche, en el hotel donde se hospedaba el equipo (que era ese hotel barato que Erokspor nos contrató personalmente), un ascensor se cayó tres pisos y cinco de nuestros jugadores resultaron heridos". El entrenador serbio daba gracias de que sus jugadores no hubieran sufrido "heridas graves que les arruinen la vida" y, para finalizar, atizaba también a la FIBA: "Gracias por ignorar nuestra solicitud de posponer el partido debido a la ausencia de numerosos jugadores. Son geniales". En las estadísticas del encuentro, puede verse que 10 de los 12 jugadores saltaron a la cancha mientras que uno de ellos que sólo estuvo en pista durante dos minutos.

articles.title: Kentucky State Women's Basketball Player from Senegal Freed After 2 Months in ICE Custody
articles.summary: LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — A Kentucky State University women's basketball player from Senegal, who was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, has been released after spending two months in custody.
articles.body:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — A Kentucky State University women's basketball player from Senegal, who was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, has been released after spending two months in custody.

At a hearing on Tuesday a judge granted a $2,500 bond for Aminata Seck and it was posted Wednesday after ICE did not appeal, according to Hishem Alsalman, managing attorney of Alsalman Law Office.

The judge found that she was not a danger to the community or a flight risk, Alsalman said Thursday.

The judge also ruled that she can continue working toward her degree and praised her for her academic and athletic achievements.

The 26-year-old Seck was detained on Aug. 7 at Louisville's Muhammad Ali International Airport as she was planning to travel with her team to a tournament.

The Department of Homeland Security, under which ICE operates, previously said in a statement that Seck legally entered the United States in 2019, then "chose to overstay her welcome in violation of our nation's laws." The agency wrote that an immigration judge had ordered Seck removed a year ago after she failed to appear at an immigration hearing.

Alsalman had previously said that the immigration judge found that Seck did not receive the notice of the prior proceedings.

She was named to the Southern Intercollegiate Athletic Conference all-conference third team last season after she led her team with 11.7 points and 7.3 rebounds. The 6-foot-4 center had five double-doubles last season and scored a season-high 30 points against Lane College on Jan. 14.

Seck also was named the SIAC Women's Basketball Elite 16 award winner. The award is the SIAC's highest academic honor and is presented to student-athletes who demonstrate exemplary performance in sports and the classroom.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark on Kelsey Mitchell's comments about treatment she received: 'As her teammate, it makes you upset'
articles.summary: Mitchell cited how difficult it can be at times being Clark's teammate.
articles.body:
During her end-of-season press conference on Thursday, Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark addressed teammate Kelsey Mitchell's comments about the difficulty of playing with Clark and the attention that comes with being her teammate .

On Saturday, Mitchell cited hateful private messages she's received on social media, as well as getting "a lot of flak just from being on [Clark's] team."

Clark said Thursday: "As her teammate, it makes you upset because you care about your teammates so much, and you don't want any of them to go through something like that. For the people that have followed me, obviously, there is such a microscope on me, and that kind of comes with everybody else that I've been teammates with — whether that was my time at Iowa, whether that's been here — [it] comes with a lot of really great things, and then, at times, there can be some negatives.

"As far as people that have used me to demonstrate racist rhetoric, or hate, or discrimination, that's not something that I stand for. It's never been something I've stood for. For those of you that know me, you know that's not what I'm about. It's not how I was raised, so that's really disappointing when people do that. ... Anytime I see something like that [it] makes me upset, makes me sad, makes me really disappointed because that's not who I am. That's not what I'm about."

Mitchell can be a free agent this offseason, and she is one player Clark wants to see on the roster going forward. Mitchell, a four-time All-Star, said on Saturday that it's too early to make a decision on what she will do.

Clark said she is going to recruit Mitchell to re-sign.

"As far as Kelsey and our future with her with the organization, I think she knows how much I love her," Clark said. "We've talked since the season has ended, and there's nobody I would want to share the backcourt with other than her."

Caitlin Clark on EPIC extension, future with Fever

Clark said "no matter what, I'm going to be here," when asked about her future with the Fever, who finished with a 28-16 record during the regular season before being knocked out by the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces in the opening round.

The three-time WNBA All-Star and 2024 All-WNBA first-teamer is eligible to sign an EPIC extension, and while Clark said she's been too busy playing golf to think about her next deal, keeping a competitive roster intact will be an important factor.

"It's just figuring out the way we need to construct our roster" said Clark, who was non-committal about whether she'll sign the EPIC extension. "No matter what, I'm going to be here. I just want to do what's best for the team and make sure we have the opportunity to be able to win championships. That's my main goal.

"Obviously, it's a really cool opportunity. I think it's something that's great that was added to the CBA to reward young players that are on their rookie deals."

Clark, if she decides to sign the EPIC deal, could cash in. But she will weigh that against taking less in order to provide general manager Amber Cox the salary-cap space to improve the roster.

"My focus is on winning. I certainly know what I deserve and what I'm worth, but at the same time, sometimes you have to make sacrifices," Clark said. "I'm not saying I'm not going to sign it. I'm not saying I am going to sign it.

"Those are just conversations that I'll have with the front office and ownership about where we want to go and what we need, what sacrifices have to be made or not made or who we can pay, who needs this, who needs that."

articles.title: Austin Reaves Says Luka Doncic Was 'Sheltered' After Trade to Lakers, 'We Didn't Really Speak'
articles.summary: Even though Luka Dončić didn't take long to acclimate to the Los Angeles Lakers on the court after the surprise trade from the Dallas Mavericks, he wasn't as open and outgoing behind the scenes.
articles.body:
Even though Luka Dončić didn't take long to acclimate to the Los Angeles Lakers on the court after the surprise trade from the Dallas Mavericks, he wasn't as open and outgoing behind the scenes.

Speaking to Sports Illustrated 's Chris Mannix , Austin Reaves recalled Dončić being "sheltered" during his early days with the Lakers.

"He was kind of sheltered," Reaves said. "For basically most of the rest of that year, we didn't really speak to each other that much. I know he was going through stuff as far as the trade and being disappointed. I was never going to be the type of guy to force a friendship, so I let that build naturally."

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

It's unclear exactly when Dončić came out of his shell, but one reasonable assumption would be around August 2025 when he committed to the Lakers by signing a three-year, $165 million extension.

There was reportedly some concern within the Lakers about whether or not Dončić would extend, so getting it out of the way had to be a huge sigh of relief.

During his first full season with the Lakers, Dončić and Reaves were closely bonded. Their dynamic was described by people in the organization as a "bromance" built on a shared love of trash talk and teasing.

Dončić's performance on the court during the 2025-26 season seemed to indicate he was more comfortable in Los Angeles. He averaged 33.5 points, his second-highest total in a single season, and 8.3 assists per game in 64 starts.

The departure of LeBron James in free agency this offseason left no doubt that Dončić is the face of the Lakers franchise. Everything they are doing is built around his strengths.

One thing the Lakers did to help make sure Dončić remains comfortable and happy is signing Reaves to a four-year, $185 million contract this summer to keep the bromance going.

Dončić, Reaves and the Lakers will open the 2026-27 regular season against the Golden State Warriors on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Praises LeBron James, 'Had So Much Fun' Being Lakers Teammates After Mavs Trade
articles.summary: While their time together didn't result in a deep playoff run, Luka Dončić looked back fondly on his run with LeBron James on the Los Angeles Lakers.
articles.body:
While their time together didn't result in a deep playoff run, Luka Dončić looked back fondly on his run with LeBron James on the Los Angeles Lakers.

"He just let me be me, and I really respect that," he told Sports Illustrated 's Chris Mannix . "And the way he approached the game with us, it was unbelievable. It was very respectable. I had so much fun playing with him. And, like I said, I think we could have made some noise in the playoffs if me and [Austin Reaves] don't get injured. I think we had a chance."

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

The Luka-LeBron tandem is bound to be a big what if among NBA fans. They were only teammates for a year and a half, and Dončić acknowledged to Mannix there were some complications due to him joining the Lakers midseason.

"We didn't really get time to practice or get to know each other or how we wanted to play," he said.

James also missed a stretch of seven straight games in March 2025, costing the Lakers valuable time they needed for their two stars to jell on the court.

Injuries then presented a roadblock to Los Angeles' championship ambitions in 2025-26. Dončić and James missed 18 and 22 games, respectively, in the regular season, and the former was sidelined for the entirety of the postseason.

If Luka had somehow found his way to Southern California earlier in his career, the Lakers might've had a longer runway to build around he and LeBron.

When the two were at such different points in their careers, this was a formula that looked better on paper than it did in reality.

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball 2026 Early-Round Rankings and NBA Mock Draft Analysis
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NBA preseason has arrived, and it brought fantasy draft prep season along with it.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA preseason has arrived, and it brought fantasy draft prep season along with it.

With less than two weeks remaining before the campaign's opening tip gets tossed, fantasy managers need to move through this process pretty quickly.

While there are a ton of things to tackle before you're on the clock, we're here to help ease some of that burden. After running through our early-round draft rankings, we'll examine two recent expert mock drafts.

ESPN's fantasy team threw together a recent 10-team, head-to-head categories mock draft. While things mostly went according to plan, there were (as always) some surprises on the board.

Giannis Antetokounmpo, for instance, lasted until the 15th pick—landing behind, among others, reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg and the post-Achilles version of Tyrese Haliburton. That just goes to show how limiting Antetokounmpo's lack of perimeter production (0.4 threes last season) and shaky free-throw shooting (career 69.1 percent) can be in this format.

Jalen Johnson, meanwhile, went sixth overall, directly ahead of Cade Cunningham and Jayson Tatum. Johnson, a first-time All-Star last season, can't match their name recognition, but he does stuff a stat sheet about as well as anyone: 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, 7.9 assists and 1.2 steals in 2025-26.

LaMelo Ball, now piloting the Minnesota Timberwolves attack, was the 27th overall pick, sandwiched in between Josh Giddey and Jamal Murray. Stephen Curry, a longtime fantasy superstar, went 30th overall—two spots ahead of Charlotte's new franchise face, Kon Knueppel, and three spots in front of Austin Reaves.

Yahoo Sports' Dan Titus recently participated in—and, fortunately for us, shared—a 12-team, points-league industry mock.

The scoring format featured several changes from the categories mock, starting with Victor Wembanyama leapfrogging Nikola Jokić for the No. 1 spot. Cade Cunningham, the No. 7 pick in ESPN, went No. 5 here, and Giannis Antetokounmpo jumped all the way to No. 6.

Jalen Johnson (No. 9) remained in the top 10, and Cooper Flagg (No. 10) joined him there. Tyrese Haliburton nearly made the cut (No. 11), indicating how much the fantasy community trusts his recovery. Titus actually made that pick and explained "I'd rather take that swing at the 1-2 turn than settle for a safer player with a lower ceiling."

Bam Adebayo (No. 28) saw a 10-spot drop from his categories-league placement (No. 18), while Trae Young (No. 25) enjoyed a 20-spot climb (from No. 45). This mock also showed more love to new Philadelphia 76ers teammates Jaylen Brown (No. 32) and LeBron James (No. 35) than the categories mock did (Nos. 46 and 64, respectively).

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

articles.title: SGA Says He's NBA's 'Best Player,' Addresses Social Media 'Narrative' About Flopping, Foul-Baiting
articles.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is undoubtedly one of the best players in the NBA.
articles.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is undoubtedly one of the best players in the NBA.

But the Oklahoma City Thunder believes the "one of" qualifier should be removed.

"I think I'm the best player in the NBA," he told Sean Gregory of Time . "I think the production that I have night in and night out is best-player-in-the-NBA production. I think the efficiency that I do it at is best-player-in-the-NBA efficiency. I think everybody picks up a basketball or a soccer ball or a football or a tennis ball to win the game, the match, whatever it is. And I've done my fair share of winning in these past couple years."

He's certainly done his fair share of winning.

Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder to the NBA title during the 2024-25 campaign as the league MVP and scoring champion who also finished in the top 10 of voting for the Defensive Player of the Year award.

All he did the following season was take home a second consecutive MVP while leading OKC to the best record in the NBA and the Western Conference Finals.

At just 28 years old, Gilgeous-Alexander's resume already includes the championship, an NBA Finals MVP, two league MVPs, a Western Conference Finals MVP, a scoring title, four All-NBA selections and four All-Star nods.

He has shown no signs of slowing down and will surely continue to add to his list of accomplishments for the next decade-plus.

If there is one drawback, at least in the eyes of opposing fans, it is the narrative that he flops and hunts fouls. From opposing fans chanting "flopper" at him to statistical breakdowns of how often he falls down compared to his contemporaries, the discourse is a part of the SGA conversation.

"Playing this game has done amazing things for my and my family's life," he said. "And if a narrative on social media is the worst that comes from this game for me, well, I'd take that a million times out of a million times."

The Thunder star has finished in the top three in the league in free-throw attempts per game in each of the last four seasons, so getting to the charity stripe is certainly part of his game.

But it is also what makes him so unstoppable, and he will surely continue to do so as he looks to cement himself as the best player in the league.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving to return for Mavericks preseason game in China after ACL tear, calf-strain 'setback'
articles.summary: The nine-time All-Star will return more than 19 months after tearing his left ACL — and some 10 months after a previously undisclosed calf strain.
articles.body:
Kyrie Irving will return to the court when the Dallas Mavericks take on the Houston Rockets in China this weekend, more than 19 months after a torn left ACL put him on the shelf — and some 10 months after suffering a previously undisclosed calf strain that the nine-time All-Star says derailed his efforts to come back during the 2025-26 NBA season.

New Mavericks head coach Dusty May told reporters in Macao that Irving will play in one of the two games scheduled as part of the NBA's preseason exhibition trip to China, though he wasn't sure yet whether it would be on Friday or Sunday.

"We will have a limited roster," May told reporters, according to Christian Clark of The Athletic . "Even with Kyrie, he is going to play one game here. We still haven't decided which one. Based on how his body feels, especially with the jet lag and things like that. It's still inconclusive at this time. We are working on different lineup combinations. But as of now, we are still not sure."

After such a long layoff, Irving said he does "feel like a little kid at the candy store a little bit" as he approaches his eagerly awaited return.

"For me personally, it's just getting out of my own way, and the mental aspect of it," Irving said, according to Kevin Gray of DLLS Sports . "Being back on the floor, putting my uniform back on, hearing my name be called — it feels like it's been a distant memory."

The preseason affair against the Rockets will represent Irving's first live game action since March 3, 2025, when he ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee on a drive to the basket against the Sacramento Kings. He had been playing brilliantly prior to the injury, averaging 28.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 1.8 steals and 1 block per game in his previous 10 contests while shouldering nearly the entire offensive load for a Mavericks team that had just traded franchise cornerstone Luka Dončić.

Irving returns to a drastically different Dallas team than the one he left — one led by a new head coach in May , a new president of basketball operations in Masai Ujiri , a new general manager in Mike Schmitz , and a new franchise cornerstone in reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg . The two former No. 1 overall draft picks out of Duke have yet to share the court in an actual game, since Irving missed the entirety of the 2025-26 campaign — a longer-than-anticipated absence that was extended, he told reporters in China, by a calf injury he suffered while rehabilitating.

"Throughout the season, I did have a moment in December where I did have a setback," Irving said . "That did put me out for about eight weeks. I had a calf strain — a Grade 2 calf strain — that was just crazy, and it kind of pushed my timeline back even more. So I had to take my time to heal."

A Grade 2 calf strain is "considered a partial tear" of the calf muscle, according to injury expert Jeff Stotts of In Street Clothes . The Mavericks did not disclose Irving's setback last season before officially ruling him out for the remainder of the season on Feb. 18 .

"Irving has made steady progress in rehabilitation and will remain actively engaged with the team through the remainder of the season," the Mavericks said in a team statement announcing his shutdown.

The NBA saw a spate of calf strains last year , with superstars like Giannis Antetokounmpo, Victor Wembanyama and Ja Morant sidelined for multiple weeks by calf injuries, and Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton rupturing his Achilles tendon after playing on a strained calf.

"There is a concern that calf injuries can lead to Achilles injuries, and that this is all due to incomplete rehab in the calf and favoring one leg over the other," Dr. Richard Ferkel of the Southern Orthopedic Institute told Yahoo Sports contributing writer Tom Haberstroh last year . "Teams are being much more conservative in returning players back from calf injuries."

The Mavericks were 10 games under .500 entering January, in 13th place in the Western Conference . A month later, having fallen to 19-31, they traded All-Star big man Anthony Davis — the oft-injured primary return from the Dončić deal — to the Washington Wizards. Two weeks after that, they officially shut down Irving for the season.

"This decision wasn't easy, but it's the right one," Irving said at the time . "I am grateful for the Mavericks organization, my teammates and our fans for their continued support throughout the process. I look forward to coming back stronger next season. The belief and drive I have inside only grows."

Dallas would go 7-21 with the NBA's eighth-worst net rating after the All-Star break, finishing 26-56 — the franchise's worst record since 2017-18 and its second worst this century . The Mavericks would receive the No. 9 pick in June's 2026 NBA Draft, selecting Michigan forward Morez Johnson Jr.

"I think the offseason gave me time to just take that moment to just reflect, and push my body to the limits that I knew were smart," Irving told reporters in China .

Irving profiles as one of the most interesting returning players in the NBA this season — a high-volume, high-efficiency scorer and ball-handler whose arrival could lighten the playmaking workload on Flagg and help a young, revamped Mavericks roster begin the climb back up the Western Conference standings.

"I'm ready to go out there and kick some butt," Irving told reporters during his media day press conference last month. "I know that naysayers or some of the questions around where I'm going to be are going to be inevitable. [...] This is a what-have-you-done-for-me-lately type of league, and everybody wants to see it up close. So I'm looking forward to being able to lace up my shoes and being on the court with my teammates and show everybody what I've got again."

images.caption: Kyrie Irving hasn't played in an NBA game since tearing the ACL in his left knee in March 2025. (AP/Tony Gutierrez) (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Defends Fever's Kelsey Mitchell in Video After Remarks on Negative Messages From Fans
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark expressed her hope of continuing to team with Kelsey Mitchell and condemned the abuse directed at her fellow Indiana Fever star.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark expressed her hope of continuing to team with Kelsey Mitchell and condemned the abuse directed at her fellow Indiana Fever star.

"As her teammate, that makes you upset, because you care about your teammates so much," Clark told reporters Thursday during her exit interview. "You don't want any of them to go through something like that. ... As far as people that have used me to demonstrate racist rhetoric or hate or discrimination, that's not something I stand for. It's never been something I've stood for. For those of you who know me, you know that's not what I'm about. That's not how I was raised. So that's really disappointing when people do that."

During her session with the media last week, Mitchell said that "showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard." She also referenced the "hate" she has received on social media:

Mitchell is an unrestricted free agent this offseason and one of the best players on the board. She'll have plenty of options if she's ready for a change of scenery after spending nine seasons in Indianapolis.

While the two will presumably have some direct conversations in the weeks ahead, Clark made a pitch of sorts to Mitchell on Thursday.

"She knows how much I love her," the three-time All-Star said. "There's nobody I'd want to share a backcourt with other than her. … I often tell her, I feel like I have the best seat in the house every single night. I get to watch you do your thing and be right next to you and be on the other side of the ball with you."

Mitchell averaged career highs in scoring (24.7 points) and shooting efficiency (50.9 percent overall and 45.0 percent on threes) in 2026. By ceding more of the playmaking burden to Clark, she has become an even better individual scorer.

As much as Mitchell is thriving in Indiana, the team suffered a first-round playoff exit for the third time in three years. The Fever clearly need to make some improvements to their roster, so nobody could blame Mitchell if she thought the grass were greener elsewhere.

The 30-year-old also alluded to the challenges that can come with the massive spotlight that surrounds Clark.

Given all of the factors at play, no team will be more fascinating to follow this offseason than Indiana. Mitchell's decision and what else the team can pull off will have major consequences moving forward.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Reveals Lakers Consulted Him on Roster Moves After LeBron James' Exit in NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are going to look quite different during the 2026-27 season with LeBron James no longer on the roster and a number of new faces arriving.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are going to look quite different during the 2026-27 season with LeBron James no longer on the roster and a number of new faces arriving.

And it seems as if Luka Dončić had significant sway in some of the roster decisions.

He was asked during an interview with Sports Illustrated (three-minute mark) how much the front office consulted him about, and he said, "probably everything" with a smile on his face.

Luka 'Had So Much Fun' Being Teammates with Bron

"I think we have a great team," Dončić said. "… I think we're very deep, which is very important, especially going through the playoffs."

James' departure was the highest-profile one, but it was far from the only one. The Lakers no longer have Deandre Ayton, Marcus Smart, Rui Hachimura, Luke Kennard or Jaxson Hayes, while they added Walker Kessler, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton, Quentin Grimes, Kevon Looney, Matisse Thybulle and Cameron Carr.

Perhaps most importantly, they brought back Austin Reaves as the presumed No. 2 option in the offense alongside Dončić.

There is no question, though, the show is going to run through Dončić.

He is one of the best players in the NBA and will likely have the ball in his hands even more with James no longer on the floor. His ability to hit from the outside should also create plenty of open looks for his teammates, as opposing defenses will have to extend beyond the arc.

When he drives, he is constantly looking for lob passes. He found success doing so with the Dallas Mavericks and will look to connect with Kessler in particular when he gets around the rim.

It is not surprising the Lakers would consult the player who is going to be running their offense when attempting to maximize the roster around him, and now it will be up to Dončić to live up to expectations in a daunting Western Conference.

articles.title: Real Madrid - Partizan Belgrado en directo | Última hora de Euroliga en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Esta es una sensacional asistencia de Maledon a Tavares. Otros dos libres de Campazzo: 15/15 del Madrid desde la línea. Luego anota Pradilla tras buen
articles.body:
Hola. Muy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a la Euroliga . Jornada número 4 de una Liga regular que se ha puesto de momento muy cuesta arriba para el Madrid y que por eso, afronta un partido tremendamente importante ante el Partizan de Belgrado a partir de las 20.45.

Resulta curioso pensar que el primer equipo ganador de un título a nivel europeo, el Real Madrid , aún no se haya estrenado en la Liga regular cuando se dispone a afrontar la cuarta jornada. Pero es así, el 0-3 del Madrid es tan sorprendente como real y está causando mucha inquietud en el equipo blanco.

Para tratar que esa inquietud no se transforme en nerviosismo y algo más es por lo que el equipo de Pedro Martínez necesita ganar al Partizan de Belgrado en lo que será su primera partido europeo en el Movistar Arena . Ya debutó en casa ante el Unicaja en Liga Endesa, pero no había sido anfitrión aún en Euroliga , así que el partido llega en plena necesidad blanca por la victoria.

Si tenemos en cuenta los precedentes, el Partizan es un buen cliente para el Madrid . Los de Martínez han ganado sus últimos cinco duelos ante los serbios incluyendo los dos de la temporada pasada. Pero resulta que el equipo que entrena Joan Peñarroya ha tenido un arranque fabuloso y es uno de los cuatro equipos que están arriba con un 3-0 de salida (junto a Panathinaikos, Valencia y Fenerbahce ).

Pedro Martínez , que no podrá contar con Gabi Deck por un problema en el hombre, decía sobre la especie de crisis europea del Madrid: " Yo no soy nadie para pedir paciencia. Lo que pido es trabajar en el día a día, hacer las cosas con esfuerzo y que estemos centrados en hacer las cosas que dependen de nosotros lo mejor posible".

El duelo arranca a las 20.45 y te lo vamos a contar en MARCA.com.

articles.title: Watch Giannis Make Bold Claim About His Ranking Among All-Time NBA Players in Speech to Campers
articles.summary: Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo offered some insight into how he views himself historically while speaking to some young ballers at a basketball camp in South Florida.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo offered some insight into how he views himself historically while speaking to some young ballers at a basketball camp in South Florida.

At one point, Antetokounmpo is asked what the campers can learn from his basketball journey. He said he wasn't a heralded prospect prior to arriving in the NBA and didn't earn a lot of early plaudits. Still, he went on to be "top 20 of all time," and he plans on moving into the top 10 (11:42 mark).

Players With the Most to Prove This Season 🏀

Antetokounmpo is a 10-time All-Star, nine-time All-NBA honoree and a two-time MVP with one title on his resume. The 31-year-old also had a stretch of four straight first-team All-Defensive nods and was the Defensive Player of the Year in 2019-20.

Even if the Greek Freak doesn't go on to capture another championship, his accolades speak for themselves.

Antetokounmpo is 24th on Bleacher Report's list of the greatest NBA players, which was published in 2025. To coincide with the league's 75th anniversary in 2021-22, ESPN and The Athletic ranked him 18th and 24th respectively.

Some may disagree, but Giannis isn't going out on a limb by granting himself top-20 status.

Climbing up the ladder will require some more work. Antetokounmpo would likely need at least one more NBA Finals triumph and multiple seasons where he collected MVP votes.

Given the injury troubles he has experienced in recent years, achieving either of those things is far from a guarantee.

Should Antetokounmpo fail to meaningfully improve his legacy, top 20 isn't a bad place to reside.

articles.title: LeBron James Reportedly Set to Make 76ers Preseason Debut vs. Nets Alongside Embiid, Brown, Maxey
articles.summary: LeBron James will reportedly take the court as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers for the first time during Thursday's preseason game against the Brooklyn Nets.
articles.body:
LeBron James will reportedly take the court as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers for the first time during Thursday's preseason game against the Brooklyn Nets.

"The plan is, indeed, for LeBron James to make his preseason debut with the Sixers tonight against the Nets. Actually a shorter commute to play a road game than a home practice for LeBron," ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported on NBA Today while revealing Philadelphia will play its entire starting lineup that also features Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

McMenamin added that the plan is for the starting lineup to play for approximately one half.

LeBron rejects rumor he yelled at new teammate

There figures to be an adjustment period once the regular season begins seeing how James and Brown are marquee players who consistently have the ball in their hands joining a lineup that already has players like that in Embiid and Maxey.

It is only natural to expect some growing pains, so any additional experience they can get during a preseason game is notable and should help once the regular season arrives.

Philadelphia has two more preseason games remaining after Thursday's contest, and both of them come against the rival Boston Celtics. It then begins its regular season on Oct. 20 against the reigning-champion New York Knicks.

The 76ers haven't advanced past the second round of the playoffs since reaching the 2001 NBA Finals, but expectations are significantly elevated after adding one of the greatest players of all-time in James and a five-time All-Star in Brown.

James himself even told reporters he didn't come to Philadelphia "to lose in the second round."

The four-time champion is eyeing another ring, and his new journey with the 76ers officially starts Thursday with his first game action.

articles.title: NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander joins Atlético Madrid ownership
articles.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has announced he is taking an ownership stake in one of Spain's most successful clubs.
articles.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is moving into a different sport altogether.

The two-time NBA MVP will still be playing basketball, of course, but he announced on Thursday, Oct. 8 that he is moving into soccer ownership.

Spanish La Liga club Atlético Madrid announced Gilgeous-Alexander has joined its ownership group, saying in a club release that the "partnership is grounded in shared values: ambition, excellence and the belief that every result must be earned."

The announcement did not divulge how much the Oklahoma City Thunder star had invested.

"I'm excited to officially join Atlético de Madrid's ownership group," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "This is a club with a long-standing presence at the top of European football, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Gilgeous-Alexander does have some connections with soccer, telling GQ in a 2025 fan Q&A : "If I could, I would play soccer. Soccer is my first sport."

He also has a documented friendship with Brazil and Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior , who attended an Oklahoma City Thunder game in December 2023 to support the superstar guard.

Now, Gilgeous-Alexander will be associated with Real Madrid's biggest local rival. Atlético has won 11 La Liga titles, the most of any Spanish club outside of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Gilgeous-Alexander is the two-time reigning NBA MVP, having won the award in 2025 and 2026. He also led the Thunder to an NBA title in 2025.

Spain celebrates World Cup win with epic parade

articles.title: Lakers' Luka Doncic Shows Off Supercar Collection Featuring Rare Bugatti in New Video
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is a car guy.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers superstar told Sports Illustrated that he's a big car collector, saying the favorite vehicle in his collection is his rare Bugatti, which is just one of 25 in existence (11:46 mark).

On the court, Dončić is hoping to steer a revamped Lakers roster to its first NBA title since the Orlando bubble. He's now the unquestioned face of the franchise following the departure of LeBron James, and one thing isn't in doubt—he'll be getting to the arena each night in style.

articles.title: Duke alumni updates: Boozer and Banchero square off during NBA preseason
articles.summary: Many former Duke Blue Devils took the floor Wednesday night during NBA preseason action.
articles.body:
With preseason basketball in full swing, plenty of former Duke Blue Devils took the floor for their respective NBA teams Wednesday night. How did they fare? Here are updates for every Duke alum to grace the floor.

Beginning with recent second-round pick Isaiah Evans, he played only seven minutes for the Timberwolves, scoring two points on 1-for-5 shooting as Minnesota fell to Indiana.

The Orlando Magic played their preseason opener Wednesday, meaning the Duke duo of Paolo Banchero and Wendell Carter Jr. were back in action. Banchero scored 11 points in 15 minutes to go along with five assists and one rebound. As for Carter Jr., he knocked down three 3-pointers and finished his night after tallying 13 points, four rebounds and two assists.

It was Cameron Boozer who opposed Orlando, scoring difficult buckets against the aforementioned Banchero in a narrow Memphis defeat. Boozer was sharp still, finishing with 16 points, six rebounds and two assists in 22 minutes.

In the closest contest of the night, the Thunder fell to the Milwaukee Bucks . That said, Jared McCain put in a double-digit scoring effort off the bench for Oklahoma City, tallying 11 points, two assists and one rebound.

When the Phoenix Suns took on the Chicago Bulls, both Luke Kennard and Khaman Maluach finished with eight points and four assists off the bench for Phoenix. As expected, Maluach was a bit better on the glass, grabbing seven rebounds as well. Both Tre Jones (Chicago) and Mark Williams (Phoenix) were inactive due to injury.

Looking ahead, former Duke star and No. 3 overall pick Jayson Tatum will start his preseason Thursday as the Celtics face the Cavaliers.

Contact/Follow us @DukeWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Duke news, notes and opinions. Follow Mack on X: @MackBaltes

articles.title: LeBron James to reportedly make 76ers preseason debut with rest of starting 5 Thursday vs. Nets
articles.summary: LeBron James and every other projected 76ers starter will play in the contest.
articles.body:
The biggest signing of the NBA offseason is ready for his debut. LeBron James will reportedly make his first preseason appearance with the Philadelphia 76ers on Thursday, according to ESPN.

James, 41, is expected to play against the Brooklyn Nets and will be joined by the rest of the 76ers' projected starting lineup.

That's right, James will take the court alongside Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe. Those five are unlikely to see significant time during the game, and might only play in the first half.

While it's just the preseason, Thursday will mark James' first game with the 76ers since joining the team in July. James spent the previous eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers, but announced in June that he would sign with a different franchise over the summer. He didn't wait that long before making his decision, announcing he was signing with the 76ers.

That news sent shockwaves through the NBA, and caused the 76ers' title odds to jump.

James and crew are unlikely to show out in a big way Thursday and are likely just looking to get in some conditioning in their first preseason appearance. The real magic should happen when the NBA opens its regular season.

The league planned for that, pitting the 76ers against the defending-champion New York Knicks in Madison Square Garden on opening night. It's safe to say James — and the rest of the 76ers — will be amped up for that.
